summary: Shenandoah National Park lookout, a wooden platform on a tree pole; the Association lists it gone and no source describes remains.

facts.design: Wooden platform with no roof, on a single tree pole, with a fire finder on top and a 12-step ladder
facts.status_note: Former lookout. Willhite has not seen any description of footings or remnants at the summit.

access.note: A hiking summit inside Shenandoah National Park, reached on foot from Browns Gap on Skyline Drive. The park entrance fee applies.

visit.trail_note: About nine miles round trip from the Browns Gap parking area on Skyline Drive.

events.note: Fire left the summit open, per a trail guide. No source ties it to the platform.

notes_for_editor: Identity rests on name and county. The FFLA point (38.2851, -78.73086) and Willhite's record agree on name and county, but Willhite gives no coordinates. Willhite's structure details are secondhand, from an unnamed park-archive photo, and he says the site needs more investigation. No build or removal date found. The 2006 fire is sourced only to the MyHikes PDF, which does not link it to the lookout. Hiking pages date from 2012 and 2017; current trail conditions not verified. Staffing unknown. No photo added. The Virginia Trail Guide also says past fire damage left the summit open (not cited).
